question.text:
Suppose $f(n) \in \Omega(n^2)$.

Classify the following statements:

  • $\text{S1}$. $f(n) \in \Omega(n^3)$
     
  • $\text{S2}$. $f(n) \in \Omega(n)$
     
  • $\text{S3}$. $f(n) \in O(n)$
     
  • $\text{S4}$. $f(n)$ has a Big-Theta bound.
     

Which option is correct?

  1. $\text{S1}$: Always, $\text{S2}$: Always, $\text{S3}$: Never, $\text{S4}$: Always
     
  2. $\text{S1}$: Sometimes, $\text{S2}$: Always, $\text{S3}$: Never, $\text{S4}$: Sometimes
     
  3. $\text{S1}$: Never, $\text{S2}$: Always, $\text{S3}$: Sometimes, $\text{S4}$: Sometimes
     
  4. $\text{S1}$: Sometimes, $\text{S2}$: Sometimes, $\text{S3}$: Never, $\text{S4}$: Never

question.text:
Arrange the following functions in increasing order of asymptotic growth:

$f_1(n) = n^{\sqrt n}$

$f_2(n) = 2^n$

$f_3(n) = n^{10}\cdot 2^{n/2}$

$f_4(n) = \sum_{i=1}^{n}(i+1)$
 

  1. $f_4(n) < f_1(n) < f_3(n) < f_2(n)$
     
  2. $f_4(n) < f_3(n) < f_1(n) < f_2(n)$
     
  3. $f_1(n) < f_4(n) < f_3(n) < f_2(n)$
     
  4. $f_4(n) < f_1(n) < f_2(n) < f_3(n)$

question.text:

$f_2(n) = 2^{100000n}$

$f_3(n) = {}^{n}C_{2}$

$f_4(n) = n\sqrt n$
 

  1. $f_1(n) < f_4(n) < f_3(n) < f_2(n)$
     
  2. $f_1(n) < f_3(n) < f_4(n) < f_2(n)$
     
  3. $f_4(n) < f_1(n) < f_3(n) < f_2(n)$
     
  4. $f_1(n) < f_4(n) < f_2(n) < f_3(n)$
